Custom CMD "ver" Command Text

entry.title: Zen Duplicate Titlebar Fix (Win10) 1.0.0
entry.content:
Duplicate titlebar buttons can occur on Zen when using transparent browser mods with DWMBlurGlass or OpenGlass, on Windows 10.
This mod hides the extra Windows-native titlebar buttons and lets Zen's remain.

Before

After

How It Works

  • Removes the WS_SYSMENU window style from Zen's main browser windows, preventing Windows from drawing its native titlebar buttons over Zen's.
  • Prevents Zen from restoring that style while the mod is active.
  • Involves removing the native Windows system menu from being used on Zen, normally accessible with alt + space.
  • Only targets zen.exe for it's main window(s), external windows from Zen such as Library or Browser Console are not targetted.

entry.title: Adaptive Windows 1.0.0
entry.content:
Adaptive Windows

(Português do Brasil logo abaixo / Brazilian Portuguese below)

English

An automatic tiling window manager for Windows 11, inspired by the Nava OS concept videos and by four tools: tacky-borders (focus border), komorebi (tiling), AltSnap (moving and resizing windows with Alt + mouse) and Loop (radial menu). Here you get all of it in one place. It arranges the windows of each monitor in a grid, animates every change with fluid transitions, and works together with minimize / restore / open animation mods: a window is animated straight to the new place assigned by the grid, not to where it used to be.

The mod runs in its own windhawk.exe process (a Windhawk "tool mod"), not inside Explorer, so a problem in it cannot take down the taskbar or File Explorer.

Features

  • Automatic grid. A new window takes a slot and the others make room for it; when a window closes or is minimized, the rest take over the free space.
  • Respects each app's minimum size. The grid reshapes itself so no window ends up smaller than its app allows or overlaps another one (for example Outlook and Spotify together on a short screen). If a chosen layout does not fit, the automatic layout is used.
  • Free resizing. Drag a window edge and the grid adapts to the width or height you chose: the other windows give way while you drag. Dragging a window by its title and dropping it over another one swaps the two; dropping it anywhere else sends it back to its slot.
  • Move windows with the keyboard. Win + Alt + arrows swap the focused window with its neighbor on that side.
  • Move windows with the mouse (radial menu, optional). Hold the right button (or another one you choose) over a window and a ring appears at the cursor. Move the mouse towards a side: the slot of the neighbor on that side is highlighted. Release and the two windows swap places.
  • Maximized windows that return to or enter the grid go back to normal mode and take their slot. Turn on Keep maximized windows maximized to leave them alone instead: they stay maximized, outside the grid, and take their slot again when they stop being maximized. A maximized window never gets the drawn border, and the drawn border and its glow are clipped to the window's monitor, so they do not spill onto the monitor next to it.
  • Animated border on the focused window: color, effect (solid, pulse, rainbow, gradient), line width, glow, corner radius and offset, so it can match your rounded corners mod.
  • Multiple monitors. Each monitor has its own grid, and windows can be dragged between them, including monitors with different display scales. It works within the limits each window or app imposes: the minimum size is decided by the app (and grows with the monitor's scale), so an app whose minimum is wider than the monitor will overflow its right / bottom edge.
  • Display scale aware. The gap, the screen-edge margin and the border sizes (width, glow, offset, corner radius) are set in pixels at 100% scale and scaled for each monitor, so they look the same on a 100% and on a 200% monitor.
  • Virtual desktops. When you switch desktops, the windows of the desktop you come back to return to the same slots and order, without replaying the entrance animation.

Free resizing: when it works

Dragging a window border adapts the grid only when all of these are true:

  • The window is in the grid: not taken out with the float hotkey, not maximized and not minimized.
  • There are at least two windows in the grid on the same monitor.
  • You drag an edge that faces another window. An edge against the screen border has no neighbor to take space from, so dragging it does nothing and the window goes back to its slot.
  • You hold the window by its border (within about 12 px of the left, right or bottom edge, or the top 5 px) and change its size by more than 6 px. Holding it by the middle or the title bar moves the window instead (drop it over another window to swap, anywhere else to send it back).

You do not have to aim at the border: with Resize a window with Alt + right button on, hold Alt and the right button anywhere over the window and drag sideways or up/down. The side nearest to the cursor follows the mouse (the right side if you hold the right half of the window, and so on): drag outward to enlarge the window, inward to shrink it. The other windows move out of the way while you drag, so nothing overlaps. A side against the screen border has no neighbor, so the opposite side is used instead; if neither side has a neighbor, the window goes back to its slot. Esc cancels.

Windows can be moved in a similar way: turn on Move windows with Alt + left button, hold Alt and the left button anywhere over a window, and drag. A floating window just moves. A window of the grid is pulled out of the grid after a short drag (about 40 px) and follows the mouse as a floating window. If the radial menu is set to Alt + left button, that gesture opens the menu over windows of the grid instead.

If you also use AltDrag or AltSnap. They use the same two gestures (Alt + left button to move, Alt + right button to resize) on every window. With both running, a drag over a window this mod manages goes to this mod, and a drag anywhere else goes to them. To avoid two tools answering the same gesture, leave these two options off here (they are off by default) or change the gesture there.

In the "main left" / "main top" layouts, dragging the divider of the main window changes how much of the screen it takes. Each app's minimum size still applies. Your sizes are discarded when a window is opened, closed or minimized, when the layout changes and when you re-arrange everything (Win + Alt + Home).

Hotkeys

Hotkey Action
Win + Ctrl + G Cycle the layout: auto, columns, rows, grid, main left, main top
Win + Ctrl + T Take the focused window out of the grid (it stays where it is and the others use the space); press again to put it back
Win + Alt + F Focus mode: every window on the monitor fills the screen; press again to leave
Win + Alt + ← / → Move the focused window left / right: swaps it with the window next to it on that side, whatever the layout (does nothing if there is none)
Win + Alt + ↑ / ↓ Move the focused window up / down: swaps it with the window directly above / below it (does nothing if there is none)
Win + Alt + Home Re-arrange everything and put all windows back in the grid

Every hotkey can be changed in the settings, and the change applies as soon as you save them:

  • Layout, float and re-arrange have their own text fields (for example Ctrl+Alt+G, Win+T or Alt+Home). Write modifiers (Ctrl, Alt, Shift, Win) and one key: a letter, a digit, or Up, Down, Left, Right, Home or End. Leave a field empty to turn that hotkey off.
  • Focus mode and the four arrows share one modifier choice: Win+Alt (default), Ctrl+Alt, Ctrl+Alt+Shift or Alt+Shift.
  • Avoid combinations without Win or Ctrl: they take the key away from every other app.

Hotkeys that cannot be registered are reported in the Windhawk log (error 1409 = already in use). Win + Alt + ↑ is one of them unless you turn on Take over hotkeys (see below). Win + Ctrl + T is also the default Always On Top shortcut of PowerToys: if you use both, change one of them.

Taking over shortcuts that are already in use

Windows itself uses some of these combinations: Win + Alt + ↑ snaps the window to the top half of the screen, so with the default settings it is unavailable to the mod (the log reports error 1409) and Windows keeps handling it. The mod never overrides another program's shortcut unless you ask it to. To use Win + Alt + ↑, turn on the Take over hotkeys option (off by default) or pick another set of modifiers for the arrows. With the option on, whenever a hotkey is already taken the mod catches that combination with a low-level keyboard hook, so the other program or Windows no longer receives it. The hook runs in a thread of its own, exists only while the mod runs, and only for the combinations that were already taken.

Radial menu: moving a window with the mouse

Off by default. In the settings, choose which button opens it: the right button, the middle button, or Alt / Win + the left button. Then press and hold that button over a window of the grid. A ring appears where the cursor is (after a brief hold, so a quick click does not flash it). Move the mouse out of the ring to the left, right, up or down: that slice of the ring lights up and the slot the window will go to is highlighted. Release the button to swap the window with the one in that slot. Esc cancels. If there is no window on that side, the slice turns gray and nothing happens. It only considers windows on the same monitor.

The center of the ring floats and un-floats windows without the keyboard. Keep the button pressed with the cursor still: a small circle in the middle fills up in about half a second. Release once it is full and the window leaves the grid (the others take its place). Do the same over a floating window and it goes back into the grid. Releasing before it is full is an ordinary click.

The ring has three themes: Liquid glass, the default (clear glass: the screen shows through sharp and bends at the edges of the ring), Glass (a frosted glass tube showing the blurred screen behind it) and Classic (a flat ring). The selection color paints the chosen slice and the highlight over the window that will receive the one you are moving. By default the colors are the focused window border ones, following its effect (pulse, rainbow, gradient); choose Custom to set the ring color and the selection color yourself. The ring thickness can be set too.

If you release without leaving the ring, the click is passed on to the app when the button is released, so a plain right click still opens the context menu. Over a window the mod manages (in the grid or floating), dragging with that button no longer works while the option is on; anywhere else (the desktop, the taskbar, maximized windows, ignored apps) the click is not touched at all. It needs a low-level mouse hook, which only exists while this option (or one of the two Alt gestures, resize or move) is on.

Works with other animation mods

Adaptive Windows works together with these two mods:

  • MacOS Minimize Animation (genie effect for minimize, restore and open).

  • Windows Animations.

Those mods hide the window and play their own animation. With the sync with open/close animations option on, Adaptive Windows notices this, puts the window in its final slot while it is hidden, and only animates the other windows making room, at the same time. Each window has a single animation, so nothing fights.

For the genie to land in the right place, while a window is minimized the mod writes into Windows the slot it will occupy when it comes back, and keeps that value up to date as the grid changes. This way the restore animation ends where the window will really be.

Programs you exclude in the other mod (for example Word in the genie mod) are not animated by it; in that case Adaptive Windows uses its own entrance animation.

Animations

The Nava OS style is the base (strong ease-out curve, new windows slide in from the right). There are also Smooth (slides in from the top), Snappy (no entrance effect) and Playful (enters from the bottom with a slight overshoot). While moving, a window keeps a fixed size (like when dragging): shrinking windows shrink at the start and growing ones only grow at the end, so nothing overlaps. The frame rate can follow the DWM (recommended), follow the highest refresh rate among your monitors, or be fixed (30 to 240 Hz).

Taskbar and dock

The usable area is the Windows work area. The screen-edge margin applies to all four sides. If the taskbar is hidden, windows only respect the screen edge. The bottom spacing setting (0 = automatic) is meant for docks drawn by another mod: enter the distance from the screen edge to the top of the dock. The taskbar can be on any edge of any monitor: the grid follows the Windows work area, and is re-computed when a monitor is connected or removed, the resolution changes, or the taskbar is moved or toggles auto-hide.

Corners

Uses the Windows 11 corner preference (default, rounded, small, square). Windows does not allow an arbitrary radius this way. If you already use a corner mod (for example "Custom Window Corner Radius"), leave this option on "do not touch" so the two do not fight over the corners.

Ignored windows and limits

  • Settings apply as soon as you save them; there is no need to restart the mod. Changing the apps that always stay out of the grid list also takes windows out of the grid (or brings them in) right away.
  • To take one window out of the grid for now, use the float hotkey (Win + Ctrl + T). To keep an app out of the grid always, write its name in that list (for example spotify;chrome). A name works if it is the program's name or if it appears in the window title. The list is empty by default.
  • Tool windows, always-on-top, non-focusable and non-resizable windows (panels, widgets) always stay out of the grid. The Windhawk log says why each window was ignored.
  • Windows that refuse to be positioned (a likely case is programs running as administrator) float after a few attempts; Win + Alt + Home tries again.
  • Moving windows with the keyboard only considers windows on the same monitor.

Português (Brasil)

Gerenciador de janelas em grade automática para o Windows 11, inspirado nos vídeos de conceito do Nava OS e em quatro ferramentas: tacky-borders (borda na janela em foco), komorebi (grade de janelas), AltSnap (mover e redimensionar janelas com Alt + mouse) e Loop (menu radial). Aqui você tem tudo isso em um único lugar. Ele organiza as janelas de cada monitor, anima as mudanças com transições fluidas e funciona junto com os mods de animação de minimizar, restaurar e abrir janelas: a janela é animada já para o novo lugar definido pela grade, e não para onde ela estava antes.

O mod roda em um processo windhawk.exe próprio (um "tool mod" do Windhawk), e não dentro do Explorer, então um problema nele não derruba a barra de tarefas nem o Explorador de Arquivos.

O que ele faz

  • Grade automática. Cada janela nova ocupa um espaço da grade e as outras abrem espaço para ela; ao fechar ou minimizar uma janela, as demais ocupam o espaço livre.
  • Respeita o tamanho mínimo de cada app. O formato da grade se ajusta sozinho para que nenhuma janela fique menor do que o app aceita nem sobreponha outra (por exemplo, Outlook e Spotify juntos numa tela de pouca altura). Se um layout escolhido não couber, ele usa o automático.
  • Redimensionamento livre. Arraste a borda de uma janela e a grade se adapta à largura ou à altura que você escolheu: as outras janelas abrem espaço enquanto você arrasta. Arrastar uma janela pelo meio e soltá-la sobre outra troca as duas de lugar; soltá-la em qualquer outro ponto a devolve ao seu espaço.
  • Mover janelas pelo teclado. Win + Alt + setas trocam a janela em foco com a vizinha daquele lado.
  • Mover janelas com o mouse (menu radial, opcional). Segure o botão direito (ou outro que você escolher) sobre uma janela e um anel aparece no cursor. Mova o mouse para um lado: o espaço da vizinha daquele lado é destacado. Solte e as duas janelas trocam de lugar.
  • Janelas maximizadas que voltam ou entram na grade passam ao modo normal e assumem o espaço. Ligue Manter janelas maximizadas para deixá-las em paz: elas continuam maximizadas, fora da grade, e assumem o espaço de novo quando deixam de estar maximizadas. Uma janela maximizada nunca recebe a borda desenhada, e a borda desenhada e o brilho são recortados no monitor da janela, para não passarem para o monitor ao lado.
  • Borda animada na janela em foco: cor, efeito (fixa, pulsar, arco-íris, degradê), largura da linha, brilho, raio dos cantos e deslocamento, para alinhar com o seu mod de cantos arredondados.
  • Vários monitores. Cada monitor tem a sua própria grade, e as janelas podem ser arrastadas entre eles, inclusive entre monitores de escalas diferentes. Funciona dentro dos limites impostos por cada janela ou app: o tamanho mínimo é decidido pelo app (e cresce com a escala do monitor), então um app cujo mínimo é maior que a largura do monitor vai passar da borda direita / de baixo.
  • Respeita a escala de cada monitor. O espaço entre janelas, a margem da borda da tela e as medidas da borda (largura, brilho, deslocamento, raio dos cantos) são configurados em pixels a 100% de escala e ajustados a cada monitor, então ficam iguais num monitor de 100% e num de 200%.
  • Áreas de trabalho virtuais. Ao trocar de área, as janelas da área para a qual você volta retomam os mesmos espaços e a mesma ordem, sem repetir a animação de entrada.

Redimensionamento livre: quando funciona

Arrastar a borda de uma janela adapta a grade apenas quando todas estas condições são verdadeiras:

  • A janela está na grade: não foi tirada com o atalho de soltar, nem está maximizada ou minimizada.
  • Há pelo menos duas janelas na grade no mesmo monitor.
  • Você arrasta uma borda que encosta em outra janela. Uma borda junto da borda da tela não tem vizinha para ceder espaço, então arrastá-la não faz nada e a janela volta ao seu espaço.
  • Você segura a janela pela borda (a cerca de 12 px da lateral esquerda, direita ou de baixo, ou nos 5 px de cima) e muda o tamanho em mais de 6 px. Segurar pelo meio ou pela barra de título move a janela (solte sobre outra para trocar, ou em qualquer outro ponto para devolvê-la).

Não é preciso mirar na borda: com Redimensionar a janela com Alt + botão direito ligado, segure Alt e o botão direito em qualquer ponto da janela e arraste para os lados ou para cima/baixo. A lateral mais próxima do cursor acompanha o mouse (a direita, se você segurar a metade direita da janela, e assim por diante): arraste para fora para aumentar a janela, para dentro para diminuir. As outras janelas abrem espaço enquanto você arrasta, sem sobreposição. Uma lateral junto da borda da tela não tem vizinha, então vale a lateral oposta; se nenhuma das duas tiver vizinha, a janela volta ao seu espaço. Esc cancela.

As janelas podem ser movidas de forma parecida: ligue Mover janelas com Alt + botão esquerdo, segure Alt e o botão esquerdo em qualquer ponto de uma janela e arraste. Uma janela solta apenas se move. Uma janela da grade é arrancada da grade depois de um arrasto curto (uns 40 px) e acompanha o mouse como janela solta. Se o menu radial estiver em Alt + botão esquerdo, esse gesto abre o menu sobre as janelas da grade.

Se você também usa o AltDrag ou o AltSnap. Eles usam os mesmos dois gestos (Alt + botão esquerdo para mover, Alt + botão direito para redimensionar) em qualquer janela. Com os dois ligados, um arrasto sobre uma janela que este mod administra fica com este mod, e em qualquer outro lugar fica com eles. Para não ter duas ferramentas respondendo ao mesmo gesto, deixe estas duas opções desligadas aqui (é o padrão) ou troque o gesto lá.

Nos layouts "principal à esquerda" / "principal em cima", arrastar a divisória da janela principal muda a parte da tela que ela ocupa. O tamanho mínimo de cada app continua valendo. Os tamanhos escolhidos são descartados quando uma janela é aberta, fechada ou minimizada, quando o layout muda e quando você reorganiza tudo (Win + Alt + Home).

Atalhos

Atalho Ação
Win + Ctrl + G Troca o layout: automático, colunas, linhas, grade, principal à esquerda, principal em cima
Win + Ctrl + T Tira a janela em foco da grade (ela fica onde está e as outras ocupam o espaço); apertar de novo devolve à grade
Win + Alt + F Modo foco: todas as janelas do monitor ocupam a tela toda; apertar de novo sai do modo
Win + Alt + ← / → Move a janela em foco para a esquerda / direita: troca de lugar com a janela vizinha daquele lado, qualquer que seja o layout (não faz nada se não houver)
Win + Alt + ↑ / ↓ Sobe / desce a janela em foco: troca de lugar com a janela logo acima / abaixo dela (não faz nada se não houver)
Win + Alt + Home Reorganiza tudo e devolve todas as janelas à grade

Todos os atalhos podem ser trocados nas configurações, e a mudança vale assim que você salva:

  • Layout, soltar/prender e reorganizar têm campos de texto próprios (por exemplo Ctrl+Alt+G, Win+T ou Alt+Home). Escreva os modificadores (Ctrl, Alt, Shift, Win) e uma tecla: uma letra, um dígito, ou Up, Down, Left, Right, Home ou End. Deixe o campo vazio para desligar o atalho.
  • Modo foco e as quatro setas compartilham uma única escolha de modificadores: Win+Alt (padrão), Ctrl+Alt, Ctrl+Alt+Shift ou Alt+Shift.
  • Evite combinações sem Win ou Ctrl: elas tiram a tecla de todos os outros apps.

Atalhos que não puderem ser registrados aparecem no log do Windhawk (erro 1409 = já em uso). Win + Alt + ↑ é um deles, a menos que você ligue Assumir atalhos (veja abaixo). Win + Ctrl + T também é o atalho padrão do Always On Top do PowerToys: se você usa os dois, troque um deles.

Assumir atalhos que já estão em uso

O próprio Windows usa algumas dessas combinações: Win + Alt + ↑ encaixa a janela na metade de cima da tela, então com as configurações padrão ela fica indisponível para o mod (o log mostra o erro 1409) e o Windows continua tratando-a. O mod nunca sobrescreve o atalho de outro programa se você não pedir. Para usar Win + Alt + ↑, ligue a opção Assumir atalhos (desligada por padrão) ou escolha outros modificadores para as setas. Com a opção ligada, sempre que um atalho já estiver ocupado o mod captura essa combinação com um gancho de teclado de baixo nível, e o outro programa ou o Windows deixa de recebê-la. O gancho roda numa thread própria, só existe enquanto o mod está ligado, e só para as combinações que já estavam ocupadas.

Menu radial: mover a janela com o mouse

Desligado por padrão. Nas configurações, escolha o botão que o abre: o botão direito, o do meio, ou Alt / Win + botão esquerdo. Depois pressione e segure esse botão sobre uma janela da grade. Um anel aparece onde o cursor está (depois de um instante, para não piscar num clique rápido). Mova o mouse para fora do anel, para a esquerda, direita, cima ou baixo: aquela fatia do anel acende e o espaço para onde a janela vai é destacado. Solte o botão para trocar a janela de lugar com a que ocupa aquele espaço. Esc cancela. Se não houver janela daquele lado, a fatia fica cinza e nada acontece. Só considera janelas do mesmo monitor.

O centro do anel solta e prende janelas sem o teclado. Mantenha o botão pressionado com o cursor parado: um pequeno círculo no meio se enche em cerca de meio segundo. Solte quando estiver cheio e a janela sai da grade (as outras ocupam o lugar dela). Faça o mesmo sobre uma janela solta e ela volta para a grade. Soltar antes de encher é um clique comum.

O anel tem três temas: Vidro líquido, o padrão (vidro transparente: a tela aparece nítida e se curva nas bordas do anel), Vidro (um tubo de vidro fosco que mostra a tela desfocada atrás dele) e Clássico (anel liso). A cor da seleção pinta a fatia escolhida e o destaque sobre a janela que vai receber a que você está movendo. Por padrão as cores são as da borda da janela em foco, acompanhando o efeito dela (pulsar, arco-íris, degradê); escolha Personalizadas para definir você mesmo a cor do anel e a cor da seleção. A espessura do anel também pode ser escolhida.

Se você soltar sem sair do anel, o clique é repassado ao app no momento em que o botão é solto, então um clique direito comum continua abrindo o menu de contexto. Sobre uma janela que o mod administra (na grade ou solta), arrastar com esse botão deixa de funcionar enquanto a opção está ligada; em qualquer outro lugar (a área de trabalho, a barra de tarefas, janelas maximizadas, apps ignorados) o clique nem é tocado. Ela precisa de um gancho de mouse de baixo nível, que só existe enquanto esta opção (ou um dos dois gestos com Alt, redimensionar ou mover) está ligada.

Funciona junto com outros mods de animação

O Adaptive Windows funciona junto com estes dois mods:

  • MacOS Minimize Animation (efeito genie ao minimizar, restaurar e abrir).

  • Windows Animations.

Esses mods escondem a janela e tocam a animação sozinhos. Com Sincronizar com animações de abrir/fechar ligado, o Adaptive Windows percebe isso, posiciona a janela no espaço final enquanto ela está escondida e anima só as outras janelas abrindo espaço, ao mesmo tempo. Cada janela tem uma única animação, sem briga.

Para o genie voltar ao lugar certo, enquanto uma janela está minimizada o mod grava no Windows o espaço que ela vai ocupar quando voltar e mantém esse valor atualizado conforme a grade muda. Assim a animação de restaurar termina onde a janela de fato vai ficar.

Programas que você excluir do outro mod (por exemplo, o Word no genie) não são animados por ele; nesse caso o Adaptive Windows usa a própria animação de entrada.

Animações

O estilo Nava OS é a base (curva de saída forte, janela nova entra deslizando da direita). Há também os estilos Suave (entra deslizando de cima), Rápido (sem efeito de entrada) e Elástico (entra de baixo com leve ressalto). Durante o movimento a janela mantém o tamanho (como ao arrastar): as que diminuem encolhem no início e as que crescem só crescem no final, sem sobreposição. A taxa de quadros pode seguir o DWM (recomendado), seguir a maior taxa de atualização entre os monitores, ou ser fixa (de 30 a 240 Hz).

Barra de tarefas e dock

A área útil é a área de trabalho do Windows. A Margem da borda da tela vale para os quatro lados. Se a barra de tarefas estiver escondida, as janelas respeitam apenas a borda da tela. Espaço embaixo (0 = automático) serve para docks desenhados por outro mod: informe a distância da borda da tela até o topo do dock. A barra de tarefas pode ficar em qualquer lado de qualquer monitor: a grade segue a área de trabalho do Windows e é refeita quando um monitor é conectado ou removido, a resolução muda, ou a barra é movida ou muda a opção de ocultar automaticamente.

Cantos

Usa a preferência de cantos do próprio Windows 11 (padrão, arredondado, pequeno, quadrado). O Windows não permite raio arbitrário por esta via. Se você já usa um mod de cantos (por exemplo, "Custom Window Corner Radius"), deixe esta opção em "Não mexer" para os dois não disputarem os cantos.

Janelas ignoradas e limites

  • As configurações valem assim que você as salva, sem reiniciar o mod. Mudar a lista de Aplicativos que ficam sempre fora da grade também tira janelas da grade (ou as traz) na hora.
  • Para tirar uma janela da grade por enquanto, use o atalho de soltar (Win + Ctrl + T). Para um aplicativo ficar sempre fora da grade, escreva o nome dele nessa lista (por exemplo spotify;chrome). Um nome vale se for o nome do programa ou se aparecer no título da janela. A lista vem vazia por padrão.

entry.title: Archive Preview 1.0.0
entry.content:
Archive Preview

Browse, open, copy, and extract archives directly in Windows File Explorer.

Archive Preview is a Windhawk mod that adds archive browsing to File Explorer's built-in Preview Pane (Alt + P). View files and folders inside an archive and work with them without opening a separate archive manager.

Features

  • Browse archives: Open folders and view their contents in the Preview Pane.
  • Open files: Double-click supported files to open them with their default Windows app.
  • Copy and paste: Select items, press Ctrl + C, and paste them into a folder with Ctrl + V.
  • Drag and drop: Drag files or folders from the preview into File Explorer or a compatible app.
  • Extract files: Use Extract here, Extract to, or Extract selected. You can also extract selected items from the right-click menu.
  • Fits Windows: Light and dark themes, familiar file icons, and optional columns for Date modified, Type, and Size.

Getting started

  1. Install and enable Archive Preview in Windhawk.
  2. Open File Explorer and press Alt + P to show the Preview Pane.
  3. Select a supported archive, such as a .zip or .rar file.
  4. Browse its folders, select items, and choose an action.

Useful controls

Action How to use it
Open a folder or file Double-click it
Go back Click Back
Select multiple items Use Ctrl or Shift while selecting
Copy selected items Ctrl + C, then Ctrl + V in the destination
Extract selected items Click Extract selected or press Ctrl + Shift + E
Extract to a folder Click Extract to
Extract beside the archive Click Extract here

The Ctrl + Shift + E shortcut works only when the archive list has focus. You can change or disable it in Windhawk settings.

Supported formats

Archive Preview enables four formats by default:

Default formats Extension
ZIP .zip
RAR .rar
7z .7z
TAR .tar

Optional experimental formats: .tar.gz, .tgz, .tbz, and .tzst.

To try an experimental format, add its extension under Windhawk Settings > Files / Archive extensions. These formats are not enabled by default and may not work on every Windows build. Some compound extensions need an available Windows preview association. Adding an extension does not add a missing archive provider.

Archive Preview uses the archive support provided by Windows Shell. Built-in File Explorer support for RAR, 7z, and TAR was introduced with Windows 11 23H2. For reliable native archive handling, use Windows 11 23H2 or newer; individual providers and compression methods can still vary.

Native Windows integration

Archive Preview uses Windows Shell for file access, copy, drag and drop, and extraction. It does not run its own archive extractor or create a managed disk cache for transferred or extracted files.

The mod uses runtime hooks in File Explorer to redirect supported archive previews. It reuses the built-in Windows text Preview Handler to load its archive interface inside prevhost.exe, without creating or changing COM preview registrations in the Windows Registry. Other file types continue to use their normal preview handlers.

The mod keeps a small amount of navigation data in memory to help when switching folders. Windows or the destination app may still create temporary files during an operation.

Settings

You can change these options in Windhawk:

  • Archive extensions: Choose the file types to preview.
  • Theme: Follow the system theme or select light or dark mode.
  • Columns: Show or hide Date modified, Type, and Size.
  • Extract selected shortcut: Change the keyboard shortcut.
  • Allow preview for downloaded archives: Off by default. This can relax a Windows preview check for some local archives. It does not remove Mark of the Web.
  • Diagnostics: Use Windhawk's built-in logging when troubleshooting. Logs may include file names and paths.

Important limitations

  • Windows preview compatibility: The runtime bridge requires the built-in Windows text Preview Handler and compatible File Explorer association behavior. It may not work on every Windows version or with every custom file association. It does not add a missing Windows archive provider.
  • Preview Host and unload: Disabling the mod waits for active workers and COM preview objects to finish before the DLL can unload. If prevhost.exe still holds a preview object or class factory (including for normal .txt previews), Windhawk may remain blocked until the hosting Explorer window is closed, a different file is selected, or prevhost.exe exits. A stalled Shell provider can prevent shutdown indefinitely. The mod never forces a process restart.
  • Broker security: Requests are restricted to the current user's Preview Host session, validated local archive paths and live Preview windows, but other code executing inside the same Preview Host remains in the same trust boundary. This architecture is not equivalent to fully isolating every preview provider.
  • Archive locations: Broker operations require files on a local drive reported as fixed by Windows, without junctions, symbolic links or other reparse points in the path. Network shares and drives reported as removable (including many USB drives) are rejected. The read-only recovery list may still display their contents when Windows supports the format, but broker-based open, copy, drag and extraction are unavailable there.
  • Cross-process controls: The interactive native list is owned by Explorer and parented into prevhost.exe. Windows can connect their input queues, so a stalled Shell drag or other synchronous provider operation may temporarily delay input in Explorer.
  • Trusted archives only for extraction: The native Shell backend does not enforce its own limit on the amount of data after decompression. A small archive can contain a very large amount of data. Avoid extracting files from unknown sources.
  • Windows provider support: Some archives, compression methods, or password-protected files may not work. Archive Preview does not provide a password entry window.
  • Transfers: Copy, paste, drag and drop, and opening files depend on what the Windows archive provider and destination app support. Some apps need physical files and may not accept virtual files.
  • Opening active content: Direct opening of executable files, scripts, and other risky file types is blocked. Extracting them is a separate action and should only be done with trusted files.
  • Large archives: Loading a large archive may take time. A Windows Shell provider can block inside a system call, so progress and cancellation may not respond immediately.
  • Unavailable formats: If the native browser fails for the selected archive, it stops retrying and keeps the recovery list when available. If recovery also fails, the error stays visible until a different selection or a new preview session. Temporary broker startup errors are retried for a bounded period.
  • Dates in ZIP folders: When a folder has no stored date, Archive Preview may show a date derived from items inside it. This is not always the folder's original date.
  • Selection limit: Native transfer requests support up to 4,096 selected items at a time.

Troubleshooting

The preview is not showing

If Windows cannot read an archive, Archive Preview displays the error and stops retrying that selection. Select another file and then select the archive again to retry.

Make sure the Preview Pane is enabled with Alt + P and that the archive extension is listed in Windhawk settings. The runtime bridge also needs the built-in Windows text Preview Handler to be available. If you have just updated the mod, close and reopen the File Explorer window. Archive Preview does not restart Explorer automatically.

A file will not copy, open, or extract

Try the same archive in File Explorer itself. If Windows cannot use the archive provider for that file, Archive Preview may not be able to use it either. For experimental extensions, support is not guaranteed.

Something is not working correctly

Open a GitHub issue and include your Windows version, archive format, what you tried, and what happened. Screenshots and logs can help. Remove private file names or paths before sharing logs.

Project

  • Author: Luiz Bizzio

entry.title: Quick Look 1.0.0
entry.content:
Quick Look

A native Quick Look preview for Windows File Explorer, packed as a Windhawk mod.

Select a file or a folder and press Space. That is the whole idea.

Quick Look docks a real panel inside the File Explorer window, next to the file list, and previews whatever is selected. It is not a floating window: it is a child of the Explorer tab, so it moves with it, is clipped to it and, if you want, shrinks the Details columns to reserve its own space, the way File Pilot's inspector does.

Folders open with Explorer's own file list, not a copy: the same icons, columns, sorting, view modes and scrollbars. Text, images, video, audio, PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, archives and everything else have their own preview or a proper fallback. Nothing runs on a timer in the background, and nothing that touches the disk ever blocks Explorer.

Highlights

  • A panel, not a window. Space opens it, Space or Esc closes it, the header has a close button for the mouse. It docks on the right, or at the bottom when the window is too narrow; drag its edge to change its width and the width is remembered.
  • Folders, with Explorer's own list. The preview hosts a real Explorer browser, so icons, columns, sorting, grouping and the Details / List / Icons view modes are Explorer's. A view dropdown in the header switches between Details, List, Small, Medium, Large and Extra Large icons.
  • A real filter, at the same level. Typing in the filter box shows only the matching direct children of the previewed folder, with their original columns, and clearing it brings the folder back. No subfolder is ever searched.
  • Text and code, detected by content. No extension list: a file is text when its bytes say so, so .ahk, .psd1, .config, extensionless files and anything else just work. UTF-8, UTF-16 LE/BE and the ANSI code page are decoded, and the footer reports which one was used, the size and the line count.
  • An editor-style toolbar. Word wrap, line numbers (a wrapped continuation keeps its number once), a whitespace inspector that draws spaces as dim dots, and alternating row colors. The four toggles are remembered if you want them remembered, and the defaults are settings.
  • Search inside the file. The same filter box keeps only the matching lines, each with its original line number, and highlights every match with your Windows accent color.
  • Documents without Office. Word, Excel, PowerPoint, RTF and OpenDocument files are opened as a zip of XML parts and reduced to their text, so they preview instantly even when Office is not installed. Old binary .doc, .xls and .ppt files use the Windows preview handler when one is registered.
  • Images, video and audio. Images are decoded at full resolution, videos show a frame and audio shows its album art, both through the same still-image providers Windows uses.
  • PDF. Rendered by the Windows PDF preview handler, the same component Explorer's preview pane uses, hosted inside the panel. Zoom and scroll belong to the handler.
  • Archives. A .zip (and any format the shell exposes as a folder) lists its contents in the native list. Formats with no shell namespace fall back to the properties view.
  • A fallback that still helps. Anything else shows the real file icon plus its type, size, modified date and full path.
  • Colors that follow Windows. The panel samples Explorer's actual pixels for the background and the text, and takes the accent from Windows itself, so light, dark and custom accents look native.
  • Explorer never freezes. Listing a folder, reading a file, decoding an image, building a thumbnail or checking a cloud placeholder all run on worker threads. The panel opens at once with a loading state, a new selection cancels the previous load, and a file that is only a cloud placeholder is never downloaded just to be previewed.

A few of the things it previews:

Install

  1. Install Windhawk (Windows 10 or 11).
  2. Open Quick Look on windhawk.net and press Install.
  3. Select a file or folder in File Explorer and press Space.

Quick Look is an injected mod: it runs inside explorer.exe, which is what lets the panel be a real child of the window instead of a window that follows it.

Keys

Key Action
Space Open or close the preview
Esc Close the preview
Click the close button Close the preview with the mouse
Shift + wheel Scroll a text preview sideways when word wrap is off
Mouse wheel / drag the bars Scroll the preview

Settings

Setting Default What it does
Shrink columns to fit the panel On Shrinks the file view and scales the Details columns to the space left by the panel. Turn it off to overlay the panel instead.
Remember the text preview options On Keeps wrap, line numbers, whitespace dots and alternating rows as you left them for the next window or session.
Line numbers by default Off The gutter used when the options are not remembered.
Alternating rows by default Off The alternating row color used when the options are not remembered.

What each file shows

Selection Preview
Folder Explorer's native list, with a view dropdown, a name filter and file/folder counts
Text, code, config, logs Text with wrap, line numbers, whitespace dots, alternating rows and in-file search
Word, Excel, PowerPoint, RTF, OpenDocument The document text, read directly without Office
Old .doc, .xls, .ppt The Windows preview handler when one is installed, otherwise the properties view
Images (png, jpg, gif, bmp, tif, ico, webp…) The decoded image, fitted to the panel
Video and audio A frame or the album art, as Windows produces it
PDF The Windows PDF preview handler, hosted in the panel
Archives (.zip, and formats with a shell namespace) The archive contents in the native list
Anything else The real file icon with type, size, modified date and path

How it behaves

  • The panel never navigates. Double-clicking a folder inside the preview opens its Properties; it does not enter it. Quick Look is a preview, not a file manager.
  • Single click selects. A double click on empty space does nothing.
  • Cloud files are left alone. A file that is only a placeholder is not downloaded to be previewed.
  • Text is capped. A text preview reads the first 200 KB and says so in the footer.

Troubleshooting

  • Space does nothing. The panel only opens when the file list itself has the focus, so a pending rename, an address bar edit or the search box is never hijacked. Click the file list and try again.
  • Something looks wrong. Turn on the Windhawk log for this mod (Advanced tab), reproduce it and attach the log to the issue. It is off by default because it adds a line for every step.
  • A document shows only text. That is by design: modern Office and OpenDocument files are read as text, so layout, images and colors are not part of the preview.

Contributing

Bug reports, fixes and new features are welcome. Open an issue with your Windows build, the mod version, the steps to reproduce it and, when it is visual, a screenshot or a short clip.

For a pull request: fork the repository, branch from main, change quick-look.wh.cpp, confirm it compiles and open the PR describing what changed and why. One bug or feature per PR is much easier to review.

License

Released under the MIT License. See the license file. The inflate code that reads Word and OpenDocument files is derived from zlib's puff.c and keeps its zlib license notice in the source.

entry.title: Gradual Night Light 0.4.2
entry.content:
Gradual Night Light

Automatically adjust Windows' native Night light throughout the evening, with an editable daily schedule and optional gradual transitions.

Default schedule

Setting Time Strength
Stage 1 19:00 50
Stage 2 20:00 60
Stage 3 21:00 70
Off time 07:00 Off

Settings

  • Off time: the local time when Night light turns off each day.
  • Stages: add or remove stages with Windhawk's list controls. Each stage has a time and a strength from 1 (weakest) to 100 (warmest). Three stages are provided by default; between 1 and 96 stages are supported.
  • Gradual transitions: interpolate strength between stages. For example, the default schedule produces strength 55 at 19:30. Disable this option to change strength only at each stage's start time.

Times use the local 24-hour HH:MM format. Stages are sorted automatically and the schedule repeats daily, including across midnight. All stage times must be unique and different from Off time. Invalid settings are reported in the mod log; an invalid edit keeps the last valid configuration. If saved settings are invalid at startup, the tool stays running without applying a schedule until valid settings are saved.

Night light switches off at Off time and stays off until the next stage. The last stage holds its strength until Off time. To fade in from almost no warmth, add a stage such as 18:30 with strength 1 before 19:00 with strength 50. Add further stages to create a five-stage schedule or a gradual morning fade.

Behavior and restoration

The scheduler runs in a dedicated Windhawk tool process. Every ten seconds it applies the scheduled temperature directly through Windows' display pipeline. It also checks after display changes, resume, and session unlock.

Settings and Quick Settings show Windows' own Night light configuration. Windows continues running its own schedule in the background. Its transitions can briefly take precedence until the next mod check. The mod pauses while Windows previews its strength slider. Disabling the mod reapplies the temperature requested by Windows' current settings.

The mod reads the current user's Night light settings and state from CloudStore. It applies all scheduled changes at runtime without writing either record. If Windhawk is terminated during a stage, the runtime tint may last until Windows next applies Night light or the user signs out.

If you tested an earlier prerelease, disable it before upgrading so that version can restore the settings it saved.

Requirements and limitations

The mod uses internal Windows Night light display interfaces and the modern CloudStore Current layout. The display driver must support Night light. The tool launcher supports Windhawk 1.7.3 and newer. The runtime interfaces were tested on Windows 11 build 26100, x64, with two displays. HDR and ARM64 have not been verified. If records are missing, open Settings > System > Display > Night light once.

Technical references

The parser and scheduler are independently implemented using the documented research below. No external helper, script, or runtime download is required.

  • Night light registry format research
  • Microsoft Bond CompactBinary protocol
  • Official Windhawk tool mod launcher

Differences from other mods

entry.title: WinPager 0.1.2
entry.content:
WinPager

A virtual desktop pager like KDE Plasma's, living in the Windows 11 taskbar.

  • Shows every virtual desktop with live window outlines, optionally with application icons
  • Click a desktop to switch to it; click the current one to open Task View (configurable)
  • Scroll over it to flip through desktops
  • Drag a window outline onto another desktop to move that window there
  • Hover a desktop for a list of its windows; right-click to add or remove desktops
  • Ctrl+Shift+Win+Left/Right moves the active window to the neighbouring desktop and follows it
  • KWin-style on-screen display when switching, and an option to hide Windows' own "Desktop N" popup
  • A pager on each monitor's taskbar, or one on the main taskbar showing all monitors
  • Can show only a few desktops at a time, scrolling along with the current one
  • Follows light/dark mode and the accent color

The settings mirror those of Plasma's Pager widget, plus position, theme and the switching popups.

The mod runs in its own process; it isn't injected into explorer.exe.

Notes

  • Windows 11 24H2/25H2 (build 26100 and later) only. Like other virtual desktop tools, it relies on undocumented virtual desktop interfaces, so a Windows update can break it. On a build it doesn't know, it shows an error.
  • The taskbar doesn't reserve space for it. Next to a centered row of buttons it shows only as many desktops as fit (at least the current one); on a left-aligned taskbar, a row of buttons long enough to reach the tray runs under it.
  • With "Hide the Windows "Desktop N" popup" on, a volume or brightness popup shown within 0.6 s of a switch is hidden too, since Explorer shows both in the same window.
  • WinPager is also a standalone app, WinPager.exe, built from the same source. Only one of the two runs at a time: if you switch to the mod, quit WinPager.exe and turn off its "Start with Windows".
  • Bugs and ideas: github.com/seanmamasde/WinPager/issues

entry.title: Windows 7/8/8.1 Taskbar Recreation 1.0.0
entry.content:
Windows 7/8/8.1 Taskbar Recreation

This mod recreates taskbars inspired by Windows 7, Windows 8 and Windows 8.1 on Windows 10 and 11. The taskbar runs in a dedicated Explorer process on a best-effort basis. Appearance and behavior can vary with the Windows build, DPI, taskbar replacement and other shell mods.

Features

  • Four skin presets: Windows 7, Windows 8 Beta 8148, Windows 8.0 and Windows 8.1, plus Custom for individual Start options.
  • Task buttons, window previews, Jump Lists, notification icons and toolbars.
  • An integrated notification area and taskbar, with a fallback to the native bar if the integrated tray cannot start.
  • Horizontal and vertical layouts, Aero Peek and classic flyout options.
  • Change notification area icon visibility using the Control Panel page that the mod attempts to restore, including on Windows 11; availability and behavior can vary.
  • Static taskbar textures and system colors; the textures do not blur live windows behind the bar. Windows 7 skin adds a cursor-following, icon-colored hover glow for running apps.
  • Local taskbar pins and ordering: the mod does not change Windows pins. Drag to an empty task area to pin; hover a running app to activate its window.
  • An advanced battery flyout option; compatibility may vary between Windows builds.
  • Optional secondary taskbars show pins, windows and the shared private tray. Secondary AppBar registration reserves work area when necessary and allowed by the shell. DPI scaling and flyout positioning are best-effort.
  • Experimental shell minimize-rectangle support supplies reconstructed button coordinates to Windows, without changing Windows 7 Window Animations Restorer. Availability depends on Windows shell-hook delivery and ordering.
  • Optional icon-only horizontal button width: native default, manual logical width, or read-only following of Taskbar height and icon size for standard registry-based Windhawk installations. This does not change icon size or taskbar height and does not hook or modify the other mod. Unsupported installation layouts use the original width.

Themes

Windows 7

Windows 8 Beta 8148

Windows 8.0

Windows 8.1

Custom

Choose individual Start options instead of a preset.

Installation

  1. Install and enable the mod in Windhawk.
  2. Choose a skin preset in the mod settings.
  3. Restart the mod after changing settings that require it.

Settings

The mod settings control the skin, Start button, taskbar layout, notification area, previews, flyouts and other behavior. Individual descriptions in Windhawk explain their scope and any restart requirements.

Behavior and limitations

  • The taskbar runs in a separate explorer.exe process on a best-effort basis. Notification-page hooks still run in Explorer, and other Explorer mods can load in the separate process. A watchdog attempts to restore the native taskbar after an unexpected exit; recovery from a hang or other failure is not guaranteed.

  • Skins are approximations; Windows 7 popup frames use the current system's DWM frame when available.

  • The Windows 8 Start corner is illustrated, not a live Start-screen preview.

  • Vertical layout, Aero Peek and classic flyouts may vary between Windows builds.

  • On first use, the mod downloads pnidui.dll, SndVolSSO.dll and batmeter.dll. The advanced battery flyout also downloads stobject.dll and an English or Italian language-pack CAB. Downloaded files are checked against pinned SHA-256 hashes. The Windows 10 1511 stobject.dll is loaded into the dedicated tool process and stays loaded until that process exits.

  • The integrated tray is enabled by default. It creates a private Shell_TrayWnd host and hides the native taskbar. Applications and mods that find the taskbar by class can encounter the private host; tray and AppBar traffic routed to it is processed or forwarded by the mod's UI thread. The host supplies taskbar geometry and forwards wheel input in supported cases, but it does not contain the native taskbar's ReBarWindow32, MSTaskSwWClass, Start button or XAML content. Mods that depend on those windows or content can fail or conflict. Disable the integrated tray and reload the mod if this compatibility trade-off is unsuitable.

  • The integrated tray keeps “Always show all icons” in memory for the current session. It starts from the Windows preference and does not write that preference to the system registry; it is reset when the mod reloads.

  • The Notification Area Icons page uses a private COM provider. The mod attempts to close its hosting window before unloading the Explorer hooks. Behavior has not been verified on every Windows build; if the window cannot be identified or does not respond, close the page before disabling, updating, or reloading the mod.

  • Keep a way to disable the mod or restart Explorer.

  • Windows 11 Taskbar Styler and its skins are technical references; their authors are not involved in this mod.

entry.title: Auto-Pause on Disconnect 1.0.0
entry.content:
Auto-Pause on Disconnect

Pauses what you were listening to when the headphones go away: the 3.5 mm cable pulled out, a Bluetooth headset dropped, a USB DAC unplugged. The action lands after Windows has moved the sound back to the built-in speakers, so there is no one-second blast through them.

It does not have to be a pause. The action is a setting, and so is whether it runs on a disconnect, on a connect, or both.

Features

  • Watches the default output device, so wired, Bluetooth and USB removals are caught the same way.
  • Toggle play/pause, mute the output, or unmute it.
  • Waits 300 ms by default before acting, which is enough for Windows to finish moving the stream. Adjustable.
  • Repeats inside one second are folded into a single action. One unplug raises several notifications, and play/pause is a toggle.
  • Only acts while an app is actually playing by default, so it never starts playback on its own.
  • Switching the output by hand is left alone; the old device has to be gone for the action to run.

Settings

  • When a device disconnects and When a device connects pick the direction. Connects are off by default, because plugging headphones in moves the default output too.
  • Audio role to watch is Multimedia by default, or Console, or Both.
  • Action is Toggle play/pause, Mute the default output, or Unmute it.
  • Delay before acting (ms) is how long Windows gets before the action runs, 0 to 3000.
  • Ignore repeats within (ms) is the window used to fold the burst, 0 to 5000.
  • Act only while audio is playing keeps the toggle from starting playback.

Good to know

Play/pause is a toggle, not a pause: if playback was already stopped, it starts again. Leaving Act only while audio is playing on keeps it honest, and the Windows disconnect sound is not counted as playback.

The mute action applies to whichever device is the default after the switch, which is normally the internal speakers. Pair When a device connects with unmute if the headset should bring the sound back when it returns.

The mod runs in a small process of its own rather than inside Explorer, and uses the Windows Core Audio API. The notification callback only wakes a worker thread; the delay, the playback check and the media key all happen there.

entry.title: Explorer Fast Navigation 1.0.0
entry.content:
Explorer Fast Navigation

Makes folder navigation faster and less visually disruptive in File Explorer by removing intermediate redraw flicker and deferring toolbar updates until folder contents are loaded.

How it works

In Windows 10 and Windows 11, switching folders triggers intermediate window clearing ("Working on it..." placeholder) and multiple synchronous redraw events from the Ribbon and XAML command bar before files are enumerated.

This mod optimizes the navigation pipeline:

  • Redraw suppression: Suppresses intermediate window clears and synchronous redraw flushes during folder transitions.
  • Deferred toolbar updates: Defers Ribbon and XAML command bar state notifications while files are being enumerated, flushing them once file enumeration completes (DISPID_FILELISTENUMDONE) or batch processing settles.
  • UI freeze reduction: Prevents the UI thread from locking up during folder switches and column grouping changes, lowering CPU repaint spikes.
  • Safety fallback: Incorporates a configurable safety ceiling to ensure pending UI updates always flush even on slow network drives or non-responsive storage.

Observed results

Real-world behavior varies depending on the storage medium and system load:

  • High-speed NVMe drives: Windows virtualizes viewports quickly, but the mod noticeably removes the transient white flicker, suppresses UI repaint churn, and keeps window headers responsive.
  • Mechanical hard drives and laptops: On rotational HDDs or resource-constrained mobile CPUs where disk seek times and background file enumeration can cause visible stalls, the mod eliminates the intermediate "Working on it..." freeze and keeps the Explorer interface smooth during heavy folder browsing and column grouping operations.

Settings

  • Defer immediate navigation paints: Defer immediate activation and layout paints while Explorer switches views.
  • Defer classic ribbon updates: Delay classic ribbon refreshes during navigation.
  • Defer XAML command bar updates: Delay modern command bar refreshes during navigation.
  • Defer navigation bar updates: Delay navigation state updates in classic and modern navigation bars.
  • Safety fallback ceiling (ms): Maximum time (in ms) to wait before forcing a deferred UI update to flush if navigation stalls or on slow storage.

Compatibility

  • Windows 11 (21H2, 22H2, 23H2, 24H2)
  • Windows 10 (1809 and later)
  • Architectures: 64-bit (x86-64, ARM64)

Support

If you find this mod useful, you can support its development and maintenance:

  • Support on Buy Me a Coffee

Credits

  • Based on the original implementation by Vivy (@VivyVCCS / enginelesscc).
  • Modernized, refactored, and maintained by gilnett.

entry.title: Volume Hotkeys & Audio Router 2.6.1
entry.content:
🔊 Volume Hotkeys & Audio Router

Volume control for games and setups with several output devices, on Windows 11 and 10: hotkeys for the focused game or app, per-app audio routing, volume locks, Deafen and a replacement volume OSD. Its mixer popup opens on a hotkey on top of any window — including borderless and fullscreen games — without taking the keyboard focus, so games are never minimized. It runs in its own small Windhawk process, not inside Explorer.

✨ Highlights

  • Game hotkeys – change or mute the focused game/app on every device it plays to, without opening anything. UWP apps and protected/elevated games are recognized too.
  • Per-app audio routing – send any app to another output device with the ⇄ button or a right-click.
  • Volume lock – pin the volume of an app or device; a watchdog restores it when a game or Windows changes it. Locks are kept across restarts and marked with a padlock.
  • Deafen background (BETA) – one hotkey mutes or ducks everything except the focused app and your whitelist; pressing it again restores every app individually.
  • Custom volume OSD (BETA) – 9 styles, can replace the Windows volume flyout for the media keys and the volume tooltip of the taskbar, draggable. Like the Windows flyout, it stays while the pointer rests on it, and the mouse wheel or a click on its bar changes the volume.
  • Mixer popup – volume and mute of every app on every output device at once, with live VU meters (up to 60 FPS while open); 17 layouts and 22 color themes.
  • Correct scaling – interface scale 30–300 % multiplied by the Windows display scaling of each monitor; the popup shrinks automatically when it would not fit on the screen.
  • Light on resources – nothing is polled while the popup is closed: the OSD and the volume locks react to Windows audio events, and the keyboard and mouse hooks are installed only while a feature needs them.

🎛️ Mixer layouts

Modern Cards · Compact Strip · Hi-Fi Studio Meters · Fluent Flyout · Cyber Radial HUD · Studio Mixing Desk · Floating Minimal Pill · Cyberpunk Neon Grid · Retro Cassette · LED Meter Bridge · Arcade Panel · Broadcast Console (dual VU) · Control Center Pills · Frosted Glass Tiles · Retro Terminal · Soft Neumorphic · Vertical Channel Strips.

🎨 Themes

Windows 11 Mica · Modern Dark · Light Fluent · AMOLED Black · Frosted Glass · System Accent · Classic Blue · Dracula · Nordic Frost · Cyberpunk Neon · Retro Amber · Tokyo Night · Sunset · Catppuccin Mocha · Forest · Monochrome · Deep Ocean · Rosé Pine · Gruvbox · Solarized Dark · Matrix Green · Midnight Gold.

📺 OSD styles (BETA)

Windows 11 capsule · compact pill · detailed (name, level and device) · circular ring · vertical edge bar · frosted glass · tactical game HUD · stealth dot matrix · Control Center pill.

  • Once the pointer moves onto the OSD, it works like the Windows flyout and stays on screen until the pointer leaves. The mouse wheel or touchpad scrolling over it changes the volume it shows (the master volume or the app), a click or a drag on its bar sets the level, a click on its icon mutes, and a right-click closes it. Otherwise clicks pass through it (unless dragging is enabled), and a hidden pointer (games) is ignored.
  • Replace the Windows volume flyout: the media volume keys and the mouse wheel over the taskbar notification area (tray icons and clock) go through the mod, so Windows doesn't show its own flyout or the Windows 11 volume tooltip. Other volume changes, such as touchpad gestures, headset buttons or laptop hotkey drivers, are made by Windows itself; when Windows shows its flyout for one of them, the mod keeps that flyout invisible (it clips Explorer's indicator window to an empty region and hides it) and shows its own OSD, which follows every step, at 0 % and 100 % too. Only the very first flyout after Explorer starts can show for a moment, before the mod knows its window. Brightness and other Windows indicators use the same window and stay visible: Windows reports brightness changes, so the brightness indicator shows even at 0 % or 100 % volume, except when the brightness itself is already at its limit (then nothing changes and nothing is reported). Airplane mode and other rare indicators shown right after an outside volume change, or at 0 % or 100 %, can be hidden as well. While the option is on, other tray apps and mods that react to the wheel in the notification area (for example Taskbar Volume Control with the tray area as its scroll area) don't get it. Volume indicators of manufacturer utilities (laptop or keyboard software) are separate programs and aren't affected.

⌨️ Hotkeys

Action Default
Open / close mixer Win+Alt+V
Active app volume up / down not assigned
Active app mute / unmute not assigned
Deafen background (when enabled) not assigned
Master volume up / down / mute not assigned

Only the mixer hotkey is set by default, so the mod doesn't take shortcuts that other apps use.

Format: Ctrl, Alt, Shift, Win + one key (A–Z, 0–9, F1–F24, Up, Down, Left, Right, Space, PageUp, PageDown, Num0–Num9, VolumeUp, VolumeDown, Mute…), joined with +. Leave a hotkey empty to disable it. On keyboard layouts with AltGr, Right Alt doesn't count as Ctrl+Alt.

🖱️ Using the mixer

  • Drag a slider or scroll over it to change the volume.
  • Click an app icon to mute or unmute it.
  • Click ⇄ (or right-click a row) to route the app to another device or to lock its volume.
  • Right-click or double-click a device header to make it the Windows default device.
  • Press any key or click outside to close the mixer.

🌐 Language

The mixer, menus and OSD use Language → Mod interface language (automatic, English, Ukrainian, Polish, German, French, Spanish, Russian). The settings page is translated into the same languages and follows the language of Windhawk itself (Windhawk → Settings → Language); other languages show English.

⚠️ Notes

  • Features marked BETA (OSD, Deafen background) are off by default. The mod adds no tray icon: the mixer opens with its hotkey.
  • "Route audio to" uses the same undocumented Windows API as the "App volume and device preferences" page of Windows and EarTrumpet; some apps only switch the device after their audio stream restarts.
  • While a game or app running as administrator is focused, hotkeys work through standard Windows hotkeys: holding volume up/down doesn't repeat there, and Ctrl+Alt combinations don't work there.

🧹 What stays after the mod is disabled

Like the Windows volume mixer, the mod changes Windows' own audio preferences, and Windows keeps them:

  • Output device of an app chosen with "Route audio to": stays until you pick "Windows default device" in the same menu, or use Settings → System → Sound → Volume mixer → Reset.
  • Default output device chosen in the mixer: stays, like a change made in the Windows sound settings.
  • Volume and mute levels of devices and apps: Windows remembers them, as with any mixer.
  • Deafen background: if the mod stops while Deafen is on (crash, shutdown, power loss), it restores the muted and ducked apps the next time it starts.
  • Volume locks are stored by the mod and are no longer enforced while it's disabled.
  • Windows volume flyout (with "Replace the Windows volume flyout"): the mod gives Explorer's indicator window back its normal shape when it's disabled. If its process is killed instead, the Windows flyout stays invisible until Explorer restarts (for example after signing out).

entry.title: Sleep Countdown Reset 1.0.0
entry.content:
Sleep Countdown Reset

Media servers such as Plex keep the PC awake while streaming, but idle time still accumulates. When playback ends and the request is released, Windows checks the expired idle time and sleeps immediately, leaving no time to start the next episode/media/exchange.

This mod hooks the keep-awake APIs inside each server process. Right before the server releases the request, the mod takes over with its own, for a configurable grace period or, by default, the active power plan's sleep timeout. After this period, if playback does not return, the PC sleeps normally.

Display timer and monitor state stay under Windows' control. While the grace period runs, powercfg /requests lists the mod's request under SYSTEM.

Supported servers

Included by default:

  • Plex Media Server
  • Emby Server (EmbyServer.exe)
  • Jellyfin (jellyfin.exe): only with the third-party Prevent Sleep plugin, since Jellyfin alone doesn't keep the PC awake. On PCs with Modern Standby the plugin switches power plans instead, which this mod can't see.

Can be added (see below):

  • Universal Media Server: javaw.exe, with its "Prevent sleep" option set to Playback. That process name is shared by every Java program, so they all get the grace period.
  • qBittorrent (qbittorrent.exe), with "Inhibit system sleep" enabled: grace period after downloads finish.

Not needed: remote desktop and game streaming hosts (Sunshine, Parsec, Steam Remote Play). They forward the remote keyboard and mouse as local input, so Windows already counts the user as present.

Not covered: Windows file sharing (SMB). It runs inside the kernel, with no process to hook.

Adding a program

  1. While the program is serving, run powercfg /requests in a terminal as administrator. The program must be listed under SYSTEM or EXECUTION.
  2. In Windhawk, open this mod's Advanced tab, add the executable name (e.g. qbittorrent.exe) to the custom process inclusion list, and save.
  3. With debug logging enabled, the log should show hooked SetThreadExecutionState for the new process. If the program runs as a Windows service and nothing shows up, check that Windhawk is allowed to inject into services.

Limitation

If the server process exits while holding the request, Windows drops it without any API call, and the mod can't see the release.
